newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian agency says arrests ITC official.
newsitem.headline: Indian agency says arrests ITC official.

text.p: India's Enforcement Directorate on Wednesday arrested a director of tobacco giant ITC Ltd and three former company officials on alleged violation of foreign exchange rules in export deals, a government statement said.
The statement, issued by the Finance Ministry, said enforcement authorities raided the premises of the company "in a major pre-dawn operation".
It said officials also searched the residences of ITC directors in Calcutta, Delhi, Bombay and Hyderabad.

"The search operations were organised and undertaken only after sufficient evidence had been collected indicating FERA (Foreign Exchange Regulation Act) violations by ITC Ltd to the tune of over $100 million," the statement said.
"The material already collected includes documentary evidence and statements of senior executives," it said.
ITC Ltd is 31.7 percent controlled by Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc. The rest of its shares are held by Indian financial institutions and the public.
R.K. Kutty, chairman and director-in-charge of ITC's international business division, was arrested, the statement said.
Kutty's predecessor, G.K.P. Reddy, who retired recently, was also arrested, it said.
The others arrested were R.B. Ravindranath, former vice-president of ITC's international business division, and M.B. Rao, a former export manager, the statement said.
It said the office premises of ITC's Virginia House headquarters in Calcutta and its global business office at Hyderabad were searched by enforcement officials.
The homes of former company chairmen J.N.Sapru and K.L. Chugh in Calcutta and New Delhi, respectively, were also searched, the statement said.
"Further arrests are not ruled out," it added.

"The evidence in addition indicates that part of the funds amounting to U.S. $4.0 million were retained abroad and transferred through a Swiss numbered account to benefit some non-resident Indians in the United States," the statement said.
The Enforcement Directorate said investigations were continuing and the current chairman Yogesh Deveshwar was likely to be summoned for interrogation soon.
ITC officials were not immediately available for comment.
